questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion uses three pairs of corresponding sides?

feedback.text: SAS uses two sides and the included angle.
SSS stands for side-side-side, three corresponding side pairs.
ASA uses two angles and the included side.
HL applies only to right triangles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion uses two sides and the included angle?

feedback.text: SSS has three side pairs.
AAS uses two angles and a non-included side.
AAA does not prove congruence.
SAS uses two corresponding sides and the angle between them.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion uses two angles and the included side?

feedback.text: ASA uses two angles and the side between them.
AAS uses a non-included side.
SAS uses two sides and the included angle.
SSA is not a valid congruence criterion in this lesson.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion uses two angles and a non-included side?

feedback.text: ASA requires the side between the two angles.
SSS uses three side pairs.
AAS uses two angles and a side not between them.
HL is for right triangles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion applies only to right triangles?

feedback.text: SSS can apply to any triangles.
HL uses the hypotenuse and one leg of right triangles.
ASA can apply to any triangles.
AAA does not prove congruence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Why does AAA not prove triangle congruence?

answer.text: Triangles can have the same angles but different sizes.

feedback.text: Same angles can establish shape but not size, so congruence is not guaranteed.
Angles can be measured; the issue is size.

answer.text: AAA is the same as SSS.

feedback.text: AAA is angle information, not side information.

answer.text: AAA works only for right triangles.

feedback.text: AAA is not a right-triangle congruence criterion.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Why is SSA not accepted as a general congruence criterion here?

feedback.text: SSA gives two sides and one angle, not too many sides.

answer.text: It is the same as ASA.

feedback.text: ASA uses two angles and an included side.
SSA does not always prove congruence.

answer.text: It may not determine a unique triangle.

feedback.text: SSA can create an ambiguous case, so it is not a general criterion.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Two triangles have AB ≅ DE, BC ≅ EF, and AC ≅ DF. Which criterion applies?

feedback.text: SAS would need an included angle instead of a third side.
ASA uses two angles and a side.
Three corresponding side pairs are given, so SSS applies.
AAS uses two angles and a non-included side.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Two triangles have AB ≅ DE, AC ≅ DF, and angle A ≅ angle D. Which criterion applies?

feedback.text: The congruent angle is included between the two congruent sides.
Only two side pairs are given, not three.
ASA requires two angle pairs.
HL requires right triangles with hypotenuse and leg information.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Two triangles have angle A ≅ angle D, angle B ≅ angle E, and AB ≅ DE. Which criterion applies?

feedback.text: AAS would use a non-included side.
SAS requires two side pairs.
SSS requires three side pairs.
The side AB is included between the two congruent angles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Two triangles have angle A ≅ angle D, angle B ≅ angle E, and AC ≅ DF. Which criterion applies?

feedback.text: ASA requires the included side between the two angles.
The side AC is not between the two given angles, so AAS applies.
SAS requires two side pairs and an included angle.
HL requires right triangles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Right triangles have congruent hypotenuses and one pair of congruent legs. Which criterion applies?

feedback.text: SAS is not the specific right-triangle criterion from this evidence.
AAS uses two angle pairs and a side.
HL applies to right triangles with hypotenuse and leg congruence.
AAA does not prove congruence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which information is insufficient to prove congruence?

feedback.text: SSS proves congruence.
ASA proves congruence.

answer.text: Hypotenuse and leg in right triangles

feedback.text: HL proves congruence for right triangles.
AAA can leave triangles different sizes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

A diagram gives two side pairs and a non-included angle. What should you conclude?

answer.text: The evidence is not enough for a listed congruence criterion.

feedback.text: A non-included angle with two sides is SSA, which is not accepted here.
SAS requires the included angle.
ASA requires two angles and a side.
SSS requires three side pairs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

What does the included angle mean in SAS?

feedback.text: SAS needs a specific angle, not any angle.

answer.text: The angle opposite the longest side only.

feedback.text: Side length size does not define included angle.

answer.text: The angle between the two given sides.

feedback.text: The included angle is formed by the two sides named in the evidence.
Exterior angles are not the included angle in SAS.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

What does the included side mean in ASA?

feedback.text: ASA requires the specific side between the angles.

answer.text: The side between the two given angles.

feedback.text: The included side connects the vertices of the two given angles.
Length does not define included side.

answer.text: A side not touching either angle.

feedback.text: A side not touching either angle cannot be included between them.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.3

Why can SSS be connected to rigid transformations?

feedback.text: Rigid transformations preserve side lengths; they do not change them.
SSS uses measurements or markings, not appearance.

answer.text: Three side lengths fix the triangle size and shape for a rigid-motion match.

feedback.text: With all corresponding sides fixed, a rigid motion can align congruent triangles.
SSS is a congruence criterion.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.3

Why does SAS give enough evidence for congruence?

answer.text: The included angle fixes how the two sides meet.

feedback.text: The included angle controls the triangle formed by the two sides.
A non-included angle would be SSA, not SAS.
One side alone is not enough.

answer.text: The triangles may be different sizes.

feedback.text: SAS establishes same size and shape.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.3

Which statement correctly justifies triangle congruence by rigid motion?

answer.text: A valid criterion changes one triangle until it fits.

feedback.text: Rigid transformations do not change the triangle.

answer.text: A valid criterion ignores corresponding parts.

feedback.text: Corresponding parts are essential to congruence.

answer.text: A valid criterion relies on color.

feedback.text: Color is not geometric evidence.

answer.text: A valid criterion gives enough evidence to map one triangle exactly onto the other.

feedback.text: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape and can map congruent triangles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.3

If two right triangles have congruent legs but no hypotenuse information, can HL be used?

answer.text: Yes, two legs are always HL.

feedback.text: Two legs would be a different type of evidence, not HL.

answer.text: No, HL needs the hypotenuse and one leg.

feedback.text: HL specifically requires the hypotenuse and one leg.

answer.text: Yes, because every right triangle is congruent.

feedback.text: Right triangles are not automatically congruent.
HL is valid when its conditions are met.
